{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} | location = 405 Myoken-cho, Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]]
[[Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] | shrine_Rank = Former prefectural shrine | founded = 795 CE (Enryaku 14) | associated = Myōken Shrine, Myōken-san | annual_festival = {{ill|Myōken Festival|ja|妙見祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ), also known as '''Myōken Shrine''' (みょうけんぐう) or '''Myōken-san,''' is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Yatsushiro City]], [[Kumamoto Prefecture]], Japan. Historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|State Shinto system]], it comprises three main shrines: the Upper Shrine, the Middle Shrine, and the Lower Shrine, with the Lower Shrine currently serving as the main sanctuary. Yatsushiro Shrine is counted among the "Three Great Myōken Shrines" of Japan alongside [[Sōma Nakamura Shrine]] in [[Fukushima Prefecture]] and {{ill|Nose Myōkenzan|fr}} in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == History == According to the ''Myōken Shrine Chronicle'' written in 1730 (Kyōhō 15), the shrine was first established as the Upper Shrine atop Mount Yokodake in 795 CE (Enryaku 14).{{Cite journal|和書|author=Hayase Terumi|title=囃されない笠鉾：八代妙見祭の笠鉾について|journal=造り物の文化史|date=2014|publisher=勉誠出版|isbn=9784585230281|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The Middle Shrine was constructed in 1160 CE (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was built in 1186 CE (Bunji 2) under the imperial command of [[Emperor Go-Toba]], with construction overseen by Kengyō Sanmi, Ōe no Ason Takafusa.Suzuki Kyō, ed. ''Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken Shrine. The deity [[Myōken]] symbolizes the [[Pole Star]] and the [[Big Dipper]]. The shrine functioned as a joint Shinto-Buddhist temple complex and was widely revered as the principal shrine (Ichinomiya) of the three districts of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita. Following the [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) policies of the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, with [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] and [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] enshrined as its primary deities.Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbun, ed. ''Kumamoto Prefecture Encyclopedia.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The annual ''Myōken Festival,'' held on [[November 22]]–[[November 23]], is one of the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''' and has been designated as an [[Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government.From the historical records of Yatsushiro Shrine. == Enshrined Deities == * [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] (天之御中主神) * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] (国常立尊) == Myōken Festival == === Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Designation) === The '''Myōken Festival''' (やつしろ みょうけんさい), held annually in the autumn, is among the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''', alongside the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.The "Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū" sometimes include {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead of the Hakozaki Shrine's Hōjō-e. The festival features a procession of floats and other ceremonial objects, some of which date back to the late Edo period. It was registered as part of UNESCO's [[Intangible Cultural Heritage]] in [[2016]] under the broader category of ''[[Yama, Hoko, Yatai, float festivals in Japan|Mountain, Float, and Procession Festivals]].''{{Cite web|和書|title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html|accessdate=2024-01-12}} The festival includes: * ''Oshimochi'' (Procession Downward) on [[November 22]] * ''Onobori'' (Procession Upward) on [[November 23]] == Himuro Festival == The '''Himuro Festival''' (ひむろまつり) is held annually from [[May 31]] to [[June 1]] at Yatsushiro Shrine. It is rooted in the early Edo period, when Yatsushiro Castle lord [[Hosokawa Tadaoki]] offered snow stored in the ice house of Mount Miroomiya to pray for good health.{{Cite web|和書|title=妙見さんの氷室祭り|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html|accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main Shrine Festivals == * Rice Planting Ceremony ([[January 3]]) * Seventeenth Night Festival ([[July 17]]) == Auxiliary Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Yamato Takeru]] * '''Inari Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama-no-Kami]] == Notable Structures == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken Shrine == Associated Shrines == === Reifu Shrine === * '''Deities''': Pole Star, Reifu Sonsei * '''Significance''': Reifu Shrine is an auxiliary shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine, revered as the head shrine of the deity {{ill|Jinchō Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of [[Empress Suiko]] by Prince [[Rinshō Taishi]] of [[Baekje]]. It is believed to bring prosperity and avert misfortune.Kumamoto Educational Association, ed. ''Yatsushiro District Chronicle,'' 1927, p. 396. == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine Official Page] (in Japanese) * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] (in Japanese) * {{Twitter|MyoukenKousiki}} * {{Facebook|myokensai}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Myōken Faith}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:One Shrine per Province]] [[Category:Yatsushiro City]] [[Category:Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Japanese festivals]] [[Category:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[Category:qq]] }} [[de:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[ja:八代神社]] {{Otheruses|Yatsushiro Shrine in Kumamoto Prefecture}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} |location = {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Myōken-chō 405 |coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |shrine_Rank = Prefectural Shrine |founded = 795 (Enryaku 14) |main_hall = |alternate_names = Myōken-gū
Myōken-san |annual_festival = Myōken Festival |rites = }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Commonly known as '''Myōken-gū''' (妙見宮) or '''Myōken-san''', it was historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine comprises three precincts: the U11er Shrine (Kamimiya), Middle Shrine (Nakamiya), and Lower Shrine (Shimomiya). Currently, the Lower Shrine serves as the main shrine. Alongside {{ill|Sōma Myōken|ja|相馬妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukushima Prefecture and {{ill|Myōkenzan (Osaka and Hyōgo)|lt=Nose Myōken|ja|妙見山 (能勢)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Osaka Prefecture, it is considered one of the "Three Great Myōken Shrines of Japan." == History == According to the *Myōken-gū Jikki* (1730), the shrine was founded in 795 (Enryaku 14) at the summit of Yokodake, where the U11er Shrine was established. The Middle Shrine was built in 1160 (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was constructed in 1186 (Bunji 2) as an imperial prayer offering by Emperor Go-Toba, under the direction of Lord Ōe Takafusa.Takashi Suzuki (ed.), *Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken-gū. The deity {{ill|Myōken|ja|妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} symbolizes the North Star and the Big Di11er. As a dual Shinto-Buddhist shrine and temple, it garnered widespread reverence and thrived as the Ichinomiya of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita Districts. In 1871 (Meiji 4), due to the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhist separation|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the enshrined deities were identified as {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, attaining prefectural shrine status.*Kumamoto Prefectural Encyclopedia*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The shrine’s annual *Myōken Festival*, held on November 22–23, is recognized as one of the *Three Great Festivals of Kyushu* and designated as a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.From Yatsushiro Shrine historical records. == Enshrined Deities == * {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == Yatsushiro Myōken Festival == === National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property === The *Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* (八代妙見祭) is the shrine’s autumn grand festival and one of Kyushu’s Three Great Festivals.The Three Great Festivals of Kyushu are the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukuoka, and the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival. In some cases, {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} replaces Hōjō-e. Designated a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 2011 (Heisei 23), it was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 as part of the "Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals." The festival is the largest ritual in the Yatsushiro area, with records of its observance dating back to 1515 (Eishō 12) in the *Yatsushiro Nikki*. Historically, the procession carried the deity between the Lower and Middle Shrines. After a decline during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, it was revived under the patronage of the Kato clan and later the Hosokawa and Matsui clans.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=About the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} The festival features various traditional floats, including umbrellas, *kasaboko*, dragon and lion effigies, and a tortoise-serpent float inspired by the myth of {{ill|Genbu|ja|玄武|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=Myōken Festival Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} * November 22: *Oshitauri* (Descent) * November 23: *Oagari* (Ascent) == Himuro Festival == The *Himuro Festival* (氷室祭) is held annually from May 31 to June 1 to pray for good health and prosperity. It originates from a 17th-century tradition of offering snow stored in the local *himuro* (ice chamber) to the shrine by Yatsushiro Castle lord {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html |title=Myōken-san Himuro Festival (Kumamoto Prefecture Website) |accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main festivals == * '''Rice-Planting Ritual''' (January 3) * '''17th Night Festival''' (July 17) == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Grounds == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken-gū == External Subordinate Shrine == {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Reifu Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = {{image requested|cat=Yatsushiro}} |location = {{ill|Myōken-chō, Yatsushiro|ja|妙見町 (八代市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |coordinates = |enshrined_deities = North Star, Reifu deity |shrine_Rank = Main Shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |founded = Traditionally during the reign of Empress Suiko |main_hall = }} === Reifu Shrine === * '''Enshrined Deities''': North Star, Reifu deity * '''History''': Reifu Shrine (れいふじんじゃ) is a subordinate shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine and the principal shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the deity was introduced to Japan by {{ill|Prince Imseong|ja|琳聖太子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third prince of {{ill|Seong of Baekje|ja|聖王 (百済)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and enshrined at Myōken-gū. While the shrine deteriorated during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was restored during the Taishō period.*Yatsushiro District Records*, Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association, 1927. * '''location''': A11roximately 200 meters east of Yatsushiro Shrine. == References == == Further Reading == * Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association (ed.), *Yatsushiro District Records*, 1927 (Reprinted 1973, Rinsen Shoten). * Shirai Eiji, Toki Masanori (eds.), *Shinto Dictionary*, Tokyo-dō Publishing, 1979, p. 340. * Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Editorial Committee, *Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Vol. 43: Kumamoto Prefecture*, Kadokawa Shoten, 1987, 11. 1096–1097. * Kamiyama Haruhira et al., *Complete Overview of Japan’s Shrines*, Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha, 1992. * Yatsushiro City Board of Education (ed.), *The Myōken Festival of Yatsushiro: Cultural Property Survey Report No. 43*, 2010. * {{Cite journal |author = Hayase Terumi |title = *Kasaboko Without Festivity: On the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* |journal = Cultural History of Festival Structures |date = 2014 |publisher = Bensei Publishing |isbn = 9784585230281 |ref = harv }} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Shioya Hachiman Shrine|ja|塩屋八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html Myōken Festival Historical Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] * [https://twitter.com/MyoukenKousiki Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (@MyoukenKousiki) - Twitter] * [https://www.facebook.com/myokensai/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival - Facebook] {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{Redirect-related categories|redirect1=Procession of the Myōken Festival in Yatsushiro|1-1=Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Star deities]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Yatsushiro District]] [[Category:Shimomashiki District]] [[Category:Ashikita District]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yatsushiro]] [[Category:Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:History of Yatsushiro]] [[Category:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:11]] }} [[sn:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)]] [[ja:八代神社]] {{DEFAULTSORT:やつしろしんしや}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)}}

The festival features a procession of floats and other ceremonial objects, some of which date back to the late Edo period. It was registered as part of UNESCO's [[Intangible Cultural Heritage]] in [[2016]] under the broader category of ''[[Yama, Hoko, Yatai, float festivals in Japan|Mountain, Float, and Procession Festivals]].''{{Cite web|和書|title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html|accessdate=2024-01-12}} The festival includes: * ''Oshimochi'' (Procession Downward) on [[November 22]] * ''Onobori'' (Procession Upward) on [[November 23]] == Himuro Festival == The '''Himuro Festival''' (ひむろまつり) is held annually from [[May 31]] to [[June 1]] at Yatsushiro Shrine. It is rooted in the early Edo period, when Yatsushiro Castle lord [[Hosokawa Tadaoki]] offered snow stored in the ice house of Mount Miroomiya to pray for good health.{{Cite web|和書|title=妙見さんの氷室祭り|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html|accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main Shrine Festivals == * Rice Planting Ceremony ([[January 3]]) * Seventeenth Night Festival ([[July 17]]) == Auxiliary Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Yamato Takeru]] * '''Inari Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama-no-Kami]] == Notable Structures == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken Shrine == Associated Shrines == === Reifu Shrine === * '''Deities''': Pole Star, Reifu Sonsei * '''Significance''': Reifu Shrine is an auxiliary shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine, revered as the head shrine of the deity {{ill|Jinchō Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of [[Empress Suiko]] by Prince [[Rinshō Taishi]] of [[Baekje]]. It is believed to bring prosperity and avert misfortune.Kumamoto Educational Association, ed. ''Yatsushiro District Chronicle,'' 1927, p. 396. == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine Official Page] (in Japanese) * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] (in Japanese) * {{Twitter|MyoukenKousiki}} * {{Facebook|myokensai}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Myōken Faith}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:One Shrine per Province]] [[Category:Yatsushiro City]] [[Category:Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Japanese festivals]] [[Category:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[Category:qq]] }} [[de:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[ja:八代神社]] {{Otheruses|Yatsushiro Shrine in Kumamoto Prefecture}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} |location = {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Myōken-chō 405 |coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |shrine_Rank = Prefectural Shrine |founded = 795 (Enryaku 14) |main_hall = |alternate_names = Myōken-gū
Myōken-san |annual_festival = Myōken Festival |rites = }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Commonly known as '''Myōken-gū''' (妙見宮) or '''Myōken-san''', it was historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine comprises three precincts: the U11er Shrine (Kamimiya), Middle Shrine (Nakamiya), and Lower Shrine (Shimomiya). Currently, the Lower Shrine serves as the main shrine. Alongside {{ill|Sōma Myōken|ja|相馬妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukushima Prefecture and {{ill|Myōkenzan (Osaka and Hyōgo)|lt=Nose Myōken|ja|妙見山 (能勢)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Osaka Prefecture, it is considered one of the "Three Great Myōken Shrines of Japan." == History == According to the *Myōken-gū Jikki* (1730), the shrine was founded in 795 (Enryaku 14) at the summit of Yokodake, where the U11er Shrine was established. The Middle Shrine was built in 1160 (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was constructed in 1186 (Bunji 2) as an imperial prayer offering by Emperor Go-Toba, under the direction of Lord Ōe Takafusa.Takashi Suzuki (ed.), *Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken-gū. The deity {{ill|Myōken|ja|妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} symbolizes the North Star and the Big Di11er. As a dual Shinto-Buddhist shrine and temple, it garnered widespread reverence and thrived as the Ichinomiya of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita Districts. In 1871 (Meiji 4), due to the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhist separation|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the enshrined deities were identified as {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, attaining prefectural shrine status.*Kumamoto Prefectural Encyclopedia*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The shrine’s annual *Myōken Festival*, held on November 22–23, is recognized as one of the *Three Great Festivals of Kyushu* and designated as a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.From Yatsushiro Shrine historical records. == Enshrined Deities == * {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == Yatsushiro Myōken Festival == === National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property === The *Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* (八代妙見祭) is the shrine’s autumn grand festival and one of Kyushu’s Three Great Festivals.The Three Great Festivals of Kyushu are the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukuoka, and the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival. In some cases, {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} replaces Hōjō-e. Designated a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 2011 (Heisei 23), it was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 as part of the "Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals." The festival is the largest ritual in the Yatsushiro area, with records of its observance dating back to 1515 (Eishō 12) in the *Yatsushiro Nikki*. Historically, the procession carried the deity between the Lower and Middle Shrines. After a decline during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, it was revived under the patronage of the Kato clan and later the Hosokawa and Matsui clans.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=About the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} The festival features various traditional floats, including umbrellas, *kasaboko*, dragon and lion effigies, and a tortoise-serpent float inspired by the myth of {{ill|Genbu|ja|玄武|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=Myōken Festival Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} * November 22: *Oshitauri* (Descent) * November 23: *Oagari* (Ascent) == Himuro Festival == The *Himuro Festival* (氷室祭) is held annually from May 31 to June 1 to pray for good health and prosperity. It originates from a 17th-century tradition of offering snow stored in the local *himuro* (ice chamber) to the shrine by Yatsushiro Castle lord {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html |title=Myōken-san Himuro Festival (Kumamoto Prefecture Website) |accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main festivals == * '''Rice-Planting Ritual''' (January 3) * '''17th Night Festival''' (July 17) == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神|1=Ukemochi|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Grounds == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken-gū == External Subordinate Shrine == {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Reifu Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = {{image requested|cat=Yatsushiro}} |location = {{ill|Myōken-chō, Yatsushiro|ja|妙見町 (八代市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |coordinates = |enshrined_deities = North Star, Reifu deity |shrine_Rank = Main Shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |founded = Traditionally during the reign of Empress Suiko |main_hall = }} === Reifu Shrine === * '''Enshrined Deities''': North Star, Reifu deity * '''History''': Reifu Shrine (れいふじんじゃ) is a subordinate shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine and the principal shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the deity was introduced to Japan by {{ill|Prince Imseong|ja|琳聖太子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third prince of {{ill|Seong of Baekje|ja|聖王 (百済)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and enshrined at Myōken-gū. While the shrine deteriorated during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was restored during the Taishō period.*Yatsushiro District Records*, Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association, 1927. * '''location''': A11roximately 200 meters east of Yatsushiro Shrine. == References == == Further Reading == * Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association (ed.), *Yatsushiro District Records*, 1927 (Reprinted 1973, Rinsen Shoten). * Shirai Eiji, Toki Masanori (eds.), *Shinto Dictionary*, Tokyo-dō Publishing, 1979, p. 340. * Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Editorial Committee, *Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Vol. 43: Kumamoto Prefecture*, Kadokawa Shoten, 1987, 11. 1096–1097. * Kamiyama Haruhira et al., *Complete Overview of Japan’s Shrines*, Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha, 1992. * Yatsushiro City Board of Education (ed.), *The Myōken Festival of Yatsushiro: Cultural Property Survey Report No. 43*, 2010. * {{Cite journal |author = Hayase Terumi |title = *Kasaboko Without Festivity: On the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* |journal = Cultural History of Festival Structures |date = 2014 |publisher = Bensei Publishing |isbn = 9784585230281 |ref = harv }} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Shioya Hachiman Shrine|ja|塩屋八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html Myōken Festival Historical Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] * [https://twitter.com/MyoukenKousiki Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (@MyoukenKousiki) - Twitter] * [https://www.facebook.com/myokensai/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival - Facebook] {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{Redirect-related categories|redirect1=Procession of the Myōken Festival in Yatsushiro|1-1=Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Star deities]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Yatsushiro District]] [[Category:Shimomashiki District]] [[Category:Ashikita District]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yatsushiro]] [[Category:Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:History of Yatsushiro]] [[Category:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:11]] }} [[sn:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)]] [[ja:八代神社]] {{DEFAULTSORT:やつしろしんしや}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)}}

{{混同|八代宮}} {{神社 |名称 = 八代神社 |画像 = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} |所在地 = [[熊本県]][[八代市]]妙見町405 |位置 = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[天之御中主神]]
[[国常立尊]] |社格 = 県社 |創建 = 795年（延暦14年） |本殿 = |別名 = 妙見宮
妙見さん |例祭 = 妙見祭 |神事 = }} '''八代神社'''（やつしろじんじゃ）は、[[熊本県]][[八代市]]妙見町にある[[神社]]である。'''妙見宮'''（みょうけんぐう）、妙見さん。旧[[近代社格制度|社格]]は県社。上宮、中宮、下宮の三宮からなるが、現在は下宮が本宮である。福島県の[[相馬中村神社|相馬妙見]]、大阪府の[[妙見山 (能勢)|能勢妙見]]と並んで、'''日本三大妙見'''の一つといわれる。 == 由緒 == 1730年（[[享保]]15年）に書かれた『妙見宮実紀』によれば{{sfn|早瀬 |2014|pp=139-141}}、[[795年]]（[[延暦]]14年）、横岳頂上に上宮を創祀。[[1160年]]（[[永暦]]元年）、中宮を建立。[[1186年]]（[[文治]]2年）に、[[後鳥羽天皇]]の勅願で、検校散位（けんぎょうさんみ）大江朝臣隆房により下宮が創建された[[鈴木喬]]編『熊本の神社と寺院』熊本日日新聞社、1980、90頁。 [[1870年]]（[[明治3年]]）までは妙見宮と呼ばれた。[[妙見]]神とは、北極星・北斗七星の象徴である。神道と仏教の両部の宮寺で、広く崇敬を受け、八代、下益城、芦北三郡の一の宮として栄えた。[[1871年]]（[[明治4年]]）、[[神仏分離令]]により、[[天之御中主神]]、[[国常立尊]]を祭神とし、社名を八代神社と改められ、県社となった[[熊本日日新聞]]編纂『熊本県大百科事典』熊本日日新聞社、1982、456頁。 [[11月22日]]、[[11月23日|23日]]の'''妙見祭'''は、'''九州三大祭り'''の一つで「八代妙見祭の御幸行事」として、国の[[重要無形民俗文化財]]に指定されている八代神社由緒書より。 == 御祭神 == * [[天之御中主神]] * [[国常立尊]] == 八代妙見祭 == === 重要無形民俗文化財（国指定） === '''八代妙見祭'''（やつしろ みょうけんさい）は、八代神社の秋の[[例大祭]]であり、'''九州三大祭の一つ'''である九州三大祭とは、[[鎮西大社諏訪神社|長崎諏訪神社]][[長崎くんち|おくんち]]、[[筥崎宮|福岡筥崎宮]][[放生会]]、八代神社妙見祭。なお、福岡筥崎宮放生会ではなく、[[博多祇園山笠]]の場合もある。。「八代妙見祭の御幸行事」として、国の[[重要無形民俗文化財]]に指定されている。[[平成23年|2011年]]（平成23年）[[3月9日]]指定。「[[山・鉾・屋台行事]]」の１つとし[[国際連合教育科学文化機関|て国際連合教育科学文化機関]]（ユネスコ）の[[無形文化遺産]]に登録されている。[[2016年]]（平成28年）[[11月30日]]に登録が決定した。 八代妙見祭は八代地方において最大の祭礼行事で、もっとも古い祭礼の記録は[[相良氏]]が支配していた時代の記録である『[[八代日記]]』の[[1515年]]（[[永正]]12年）に記述がある{{sfn|早瀬 |2014|pp=139-141}}。当時は下宮と中宮のあいだで神輿の神幸が行われていた。[[安土桃山時代]]に妙見宮が衰退し祭礼が途絶えた時期があったが、[[加藤氏#道長流加藤氏|加藤氏]]支配の時代に復興が図られた。[[1632年]]（[[寛永]]9年）に八代に入った[[細川忠興|細川三斎]]より神輿など祭礼道具の寄進を受け、その後の領主[[松井氏]]に妙見宮の保護が引き継がれた{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?（八代市HP） |accessdate=2016-04-22}}。 御旅所である[[塩屋八幡宮]]まで「'''お下り'''」され、一泊される。翌日、八代神社まで「'''お上り'''」の神幸で、神輿、神主、社僧、鉄砲、神馬や、八代独自の[[山車]]である笠鉾、[[長崎くんち]]風の獅子、妙見伝説にちなんだ亀蛇（[[玄武]]）など、江戸時代後期よりほぼ変わらないさまざまな[[風流]]物が行列をともにする{{sfn|早瀬 |2014|pp=139-141}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=妙見宮祭礼神幸行列関係資料（八代市HP） |accessdate=2016-04-22}}。 * お下り[[11月22日]]、お上り[[11月23日]]。 == 氷室祭 == '''氷室祭'''（ひむろまつり、ひむろさい）とは、八代神社で毎年[[5月31日]]から[[6月1日]]（氷朔日）にかけて執り行われるお祭りのこと。[[江戸時代]]初期、八代城主[[細川忠興]]が、八代神社に参拝した際、無病息災を祈念して八代の三室山の[[氷室]]に貯蔵してあった雪を奉納した事に由来すると伝わる{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html |title=妙見さんの氷室祭り（熊本県HP） |accessdate=2014-02-12}}。 雪の塊を模した雪餅（[[米粉]]を水で練り、[[蒸籠]]で蒸した餅菓子）を、お供えしたり食べたりする。無病息災を祈願して、特に還暦、厄入り・厄明けなど人生の節目に当たる人々が大勢参拝する{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kininaru-k.jp/2008/back_doc/05/0529/syoku.html |title=氷室祭の名物 雪餅（熊本県HP） |accessdate=2014-02-12}}。 == 主な例祭日 == * 御田植神事 :[[1月3日]]。お田植え祭り。 * 十七夜祭 :[[7月17日]] == 境内社 == * [[大宮神社]] :祭神 - [[日本武尊]]。 * [[稲荷神社]] :祭神 - [[保食神]]。 == 境内 == * 妙見宮の六地蔵幢 == 境外末社 == {{神社 |名称 = 霊符神社 |画像 = {{画像募集中|cat=八代市}} |所在地 = [[熊本県]][[八代市]][[妙見町 (八代市)|妙見町]] | 緯度度 = | 経度度 = |祭神 = [[北辰星]]・[[霊符尊星]] |社格 = [[鎮宅霊符神]]の総本社 |創建 = （伝）[[推古天皇]]年間 |本殿 = |別名 = |例祭 = |神事 = }} === 霊符神社 === * 祭神 - 北辰星・霊符尊星 * 由緒 - 霊符神社（れいふじんじゃ）は八代神社の末社、鎮宅霊符神の総本社。[[推古天皇]]のころ、[[百済|百済国]][[聖王 (百済)|聖明王]]の第3王子[[琳聖太子]]が八代に日本最初の霊符神を伝え、[[白木山神宮寺]]（妙見宮の神宮寺）に鎮座した。信仰すれば、除災興栄、富貴反映を得るという。明治維新後[[廃仏毀釈]]で荒廃したが、大正年代に再興熊本県教育会・石川愛郷編纂『八代郡誌』1927年（1973年再発行、臨川書店）、396-407頁。 * 所在地 - 八代神社東方約200メートル == 出典・脚注 == == 参考文献 == * 熊本県教育会・石川愛郷編纂『八代郡誌』1927年、（1973年再刊、[[臨川書店]]） * 白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』[[東京堂出版]]、1979年、340頁 * 角川日本地名大辞典編纂委員会編『角川日本地名大辞典43 熊本県』[[角川書店]]、1987年、1096-1097頁 * [[上山春平]]他『日本神社総覧』[[新人物往来社]]、1992年 * {{混同|八代宮}} {{神社 |名称 = 八代神社 |画像 = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} |所在地 = [[熊本県]][[八代市]]妙見町405 |位置 = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[天之御中主神]]
[[国常立尊]] |社格 = 県社 |創建 = 795年（延暦14年） |本殿 = |別名 = 妙見宮
妙見さん |例祭 = 妙見祭 |神事 = }} '''八代神社'''（やつしろじんじゃ）は、[[熊本県]][[八代市]]妙見町にある[[神社]]である。'''妙見宮'''（みょうけんぐう）、妙見さん。旧[[近代社格制度|社格]]は県社。上宮、中宮、下宮の三宮からなるが、現在は下宮が本宮である。福島県の[[相馬中村神社|相馬妙見]]、大阪府の[[妙見山 (能勢)|能勢妙見]]と並んで、'''日本三大妙見'''の一つといわれる。 == 由緒 == 1730年（[[享保]]15年）に書かれた『妙見宮実紀』によれば{{sfn|早瀬 |2014|pp=139-141}}、[[795年]]（[[延暦]]14年）、横岳頂上に上宮を創祀。[[1160年]]（[[永暦]]元年）、中宮を建立。[[1186年]]（[[文治]]2年）に、[[後鳥羽天皇]]の勅願で、検校散位（けんぎょうさんみ）大江朝臣隆房により下宮が創建された[[鈴木喬]]編『熊本の神社と寺院』熊本日日新聞社、1980、90頁。 [[1870年]]（[[明治3年]]）までは妙見宮と呼ばれた。[[妙見]]神とは、北極星・北斗七星の象徴である。神道と仏教の両部の宮寺で、広く崇敬を受け、八代、下益城、芦北三郡の一の宮として栄えた。[[1871年]]（[[明治4年]]）、[[神仏分離令]]により、[[天之御中主神]]、[[国常立尊]]を祭神とし、社名を八代神社と改められ、県社となった[[熊本日日新聞]]編纂『熊本県大百科事典』熊本日日新聞社、1982、456頁。 [[11月22日]]、[[11月23日|23日]]の'''妙見祭'''は、'''九州三大祭り'''の一つで「八代妙見祭の御幸行事」として、国の[[重要無形民俗文化財]]に指定されている八代神社由緒書より。 == 御祭神 == * [[天之御中主神]] * [[国常立尊]] == 八代妙見祭 == === 重要無形民俗文化財（国指定） === '''八代妙見祭'''（やつしろ みょうけんさい）は、八代神社の秋の[[例大祭]]であり、'''九州三大祭の一つ'''である九州三大祭とは、[[鎮西大社諏訪神社|長崎諏訪神社]][[長崎くんち|おくんち]]、[[筥崎宮|福岡筥崎宮]][[放生会]]、八代神社妙見祭。なお、福岡筥崎宮放生会ではなく、[[博多祇園山笠]]の場合もある。。「八代妙見祭の御幸行事」として、国の[[重要無形民俗文化財]]に指定されている。[[平成23年|2011年]]（平成23年）[[3月9日]]指定。「[[山・鉾・屋台行事]]」の１つとし[[国際連合教育科学文化機関|て国際連合教育科学文化機関]]（ユネスコ）の[[無形文化遺産]]に登録されている。[[2016年]]（平成28年）[[11月30日]]に登録が決定した。 八代妙見祭は八代地方において最大の祭礼行事で、もっとも古い祭礼の記録は[[相良氏]]が支配していた時代の記録である『[[八代日記]]』の[[1515年]]（[[永正]]12年）に記述がある{{sfn|早瀬 |2014|pp=139-141}}。当時は下宮と中宮のあいだで神輿の神幸が行われていた。[[安土桃山時代]]に妙見宮が衰退し祭礼が途絶えた時期があったが、[[加藤氏#道長流加藤氏|加藤氏]]支配の時代に復興が図られた。[[1632年]]（[[寛永]]9年）に八代に入った[[細川忠興|細川三斎]]より神輿など祭礼道具の寄進を受け、その後の領主[[松井氏]]に妙見宮の保護が引き継がれた{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?（八代市HP） |accessdate=2016-04-22}}。 御旅所である[[塩屋八幡宮]]まで「'''お下り'''」され、一泊される。翌日、八代神社まで「'''お上り'''」の神幸で、神輿、神主、社僧、鉄砲、神馬や、八代独自の[[山車]]である笠鉾、[[長崎くんち]]風の獅子、妙見伝説にちなんだ亀蛇（[[玄武]]）など、江戸時代後期よりほぼ変わらないさまざまな[[風流]]物が行列をともにする{{sfn|早瀬 |2014|pp=139-141}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=妙見宮祭礼神幸行列関係資料（八代市HP） |accessdate=2016-04-22}}。 * お下り[[11月22日]]、お上り[[11月23日]]。 == 氷室祭 == '''氷室祭'''（ひむろまつり、ひむろさい）とは、八代神社で毎年[[5月31日]]から[[6月1日]]（氷朔日）にかけて執り行われるお祭りのこと。[[江戸時代]]初期、八代城主[[細川忠興]]が、八代神社に参拝した際、無病息災を祈念して八代の三室山の[[氷室]]に貯蔵してあった雪を奉納した事に由来すると伝わる{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html |title=妙見さんの氷室祭り（熊本県HP） |accessdate=2014-02-12}}。 雪の塊を模した雪餅（[[米粉]]を水で練り、[[蒸籠]]で蒸した餅菓子）を、お供えしたり食べたりする。無病息災を祈願して、特に還暦、厄入り・厄明けなど人生の節目に当たる人々が大勢参拝する{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.kininaru-k.jp/2008/back_doc/05/0529/syoku.html |title=氷室祭の名物 雪餅（熊本県HP） |accessdate=2014-02-12}}。 == 主な例祭日 == * 御田植神事 :[[1月3日]]。お田植え祭り。 * 十七夜祭 :[[7月17日]] == 境内社 == * [[大宮神社]] :祭神 - [[日本武尊]]。 * [[稲荷神社]] :祭神 - [[保食神]]。 == 境内 == * 妙見宮の六地蔵幢 == 境外末社 == {{神社 |名称 = 霊符神社 |画像 = {{画像募集中|cat=八代市}} |所在地 = [[熊本県]][[八代市]][[妙見町 (八代市)|妙見町]] | 緯度度 = | 経度度 = |祭神 = [[北辰星]]・[[霊符尊星]] |社格 = [[鎮宅霊符神]]の総本社 |創建 = （伝）[[推古天皇]]年間 |本殿 = |別名 = |例祭 = |神事 = }} === 霊符神社 === * 祭神 - 北辰星・霊符尊星 * 由緒 - 霊符神社（れいふじんじゃ）は八代神社の末社、鎮宅霊符神の総本社。[[推古天皇]]のころ、[[百済|百済国]][[聖王 (百済)|聖明王]]の第3王子[[琳聖太子]]が八代に日本最初の霊符神を伝え、[[白木山神宮寺]]（妙見宮の神宮寺）に鎮座した。信仰すれば、除災興栄、富貴反映を得るという。明治維新後[[廃仏毀釈]]で荒廃したが、大正年代に再興熊本県教育会・石川愛郷編纂『八代郡誌』1927年（1973年再発行、臨川書店）、396-407頁。 * 所在地 - 八代神社東方約200メートル == 出典・脚注 == == 参考文献 == * 熊本県教育会・石川愛郷編纂『八代郡誌』1927年、（1973年再刊、[[臨川書店]]） * 白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』[[東京堂出版]]、1979年、340頁 * 角川日本地名大辞典編纂委員会編『角川日本地名大辞典43 熊本県』[[角川書店]]、1987年、1096-1097頁 * [[上山春平]]他『日本神社総覧』[[新人物往来社]]、1992年 * 妙見宮祭礼神幸行列関係資料]（八代市公式HP） * [http://www.myouken.com/ 八代妙見祭公式ホームページ] * [https://twitter.com/MyoukenKousiki 八代妙見祭](@MyoukenKousiki)-[[Twitter]] * [https://twitter.com/myoukenhoukago 八代妙見祭](@myoukenhoukago)-[[Twitter]] * [https://www.facebook.com/myokensai/ 八代妙見祭]-[[Facebook]] {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{リダイレクトの所属カテゴリ|redirect1=八代妙見祭の神幸行事|1-1=山・鉾・屋台行事}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やつしろしんしや}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} | location = 405 Myoken-cho, Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]]
[[Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] | shrine_Rank = Former prefectural shrine | founded = 795 CE (Enryaku 14) | associated = Myōken Shrine, Myōken-san | annual_festival = {{ill|Myōken Festival|ja|妙見祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ), also known as '''Myōken Shrine''' (みょうけんぐう) or '''Myōken-san,''' is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Yatsushiro City]], [[Kumamoto Prefecture]], Japan. Historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|State Shinto system]], it comprises three main shrines: the Upper Shrine, the Middle Shrine, and the Lower Shrine, with the Lower Shrine currently serving as the main sanctuary. Yatsushiro Shrine is counted among the "Three Great Myōken Shrines" of Japan alongside [[Sōma Nakamura Shrine]] in [[Fukushima Prefecture]] and {{ill|Nose Myōkenzan|fr}} in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == History == According to the ''Myōken Shrine Chronicle'' written in 1730 (Kyōhō 15), the shrine was first established as the Upper Shrine atop Mount Yokodake in 795 CE (Enryaku 14).{{Cite journal|和書|author=Hayase Terumi|title=囃されない笠鉾：八代妙見祭の笠鉾について|journal=造り物の文化史|date=2014|publisher=勉誠出版|isbn=9784585230281|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The Middle Shrine was constructed in 1160 CE (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was built in 1186 CE (Bunji 2) under the imperial command of [[Emperor Go-Toba]], with construction overseen by Kengyō Sanmi, Ōe no Ason Takafusa.Suzuki Kyō, ed. ''Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken Shrine. The deity [[Myōken]] symbolizes the [[Pole Star]] and the [[Big Dipper]]. The shrine functioned as a joint Shinto-Buddhist temple complex and was widely revered as the principal shrine (Ichinomiya) of the three districts of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita. Following the [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) policies of the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, with [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] and [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] enshrined as its primary deities.Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbun, ed. ''Kumamoto Prefecture Encyclopedia.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The annual ''Myōken Festival,'' held on [[November 22]]–[[November 23]], is one of the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''' and has been designated as an [[Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government.From the historical records of Yatsushiro Shrine. == Enshrined Deities == * [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] (天之御中主神) * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] (国常立尊) == Myōken Festival == === Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Designation) === The '''Myōken Festival''' (やつしろ みょうけんさい), held annually in the autumn, is among the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''', alongside the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.The "Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū" sometimes include {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead of the Hakozaki Shrine's Hōjō-e. The festival features a procession of floats and other ceremonial objects, some of which date back to the late Edo period. It was registered as part of UNESCO's [[Intangible Cultural Heritage]] in [[2016]] under the broader category of ''[[Yama, Hoko, Yatai, float festivals in Japan|Mountain, Float, and Procession Festivals]].''{{Cite web|和書|title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html|accessdate=2024-01-12}} The festival includes: * ''Oshimochi'' (Procession Downward) on [[November 22]] * ''Onobori'' (Procession Upward) on [[November 23]] == Himuro Festival == The '''Himuro Festival''' (ひむろまつり) is held annually from [[May 31]] to [[June 1]] at Yatsushiro Shrine. It is rooted in the early Edo period, when Yatsushiro Castle lord [[Hosokawa Tadaoki]] offered snow stored in the ice house of Mount Miroomiya to pray for good health.{{Cite web|和書|title=妙見さんの氷室祭り|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html|accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main Shrine Festivals == * Rice Planting Ceremony ([[January 3]]) * Seventeenth Night Festival ([[July 17]]) == Auxiliary Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Yamato Takeru]] * '''Inari Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama-no-Kami]] == Notable Structures == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken Shrine == Associated Shrines == === Reifu Shrine === * '''Deities''': Pole Star, Reifu Sonsei * '''Significance''': Reifu Shrine is an auxiliary shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine, revered as the head shrine of the deity {{ill|Jinchō Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of [[Empress Suiko]] by Prince [[Rinshō Taishi]] of [[Baekje]]. It is believed to bring prosperity and avert misfortune.Kumamoto Educational Association, ed. ''Yatsushiro District Chronicle,'' 1927, p. 396. == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine Official Page] (in Japanese) * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] (in Japanese) * {{Twitter|MyoukenKousiki}} * {{Facebook|myokensai}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Myōken Faith}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:One Shrine per Province]] [[Category:Yatsushiro City]] [[Category:Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Japanese festivals]] [[Category:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[Category:qq]] }} [[de:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[ja:八代神社]] {{Otheruses|Yatsushiro Shrine in Kumamoto Prefecture}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} |location = {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Myōken-chō 405 |coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |shrine_Rank = Prefectural Shrine |founded = 795 (Enryaku 14) |main_hall = |alternate_names = Myōken-gū
Myōken-san |annual_festival = Myōken Festival |rites = }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Commonly known as '''Myōken-gū''' (妙見宮) or '''Myōken-san''', it was historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine comprises three precincts: the U11er Shrine (Kamimiya), Middle Shrine (Nakamiya), and Lower Shrine (Shimomiya). Currently, the Lower Shrine serves as the main shrine. Alongside {{ill|Sōma Myōken|ja|相馬妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukushima Prefecture and {{ill|Myōkenzan (Osaka and Hyōgo)|lt=Nose Myōken|ja|妙見山 (能勢)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Osaka Prefecture, it is considered one of the "Three Great Myōken Shrines of Japan." == History == According to the *Myōken-gū Jikki* (1730), the shrine was founded in 795 (Enryaku 14) at the summit of Yokodake, where the U11er Shrine was established. The Middle Shrine was built in 1160 (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was constructed in 1186 (Bunji 2) as an imperial prayer offering by Emperor Go-Toba, under the direction of Lord Ōe Takafusa.Takashi Suzuki (ed.), *Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken-gū. The deity {{ill|Myōken|ja|妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} symbolizes the North Star and the Big Di11er. As a dual Shinto-Buddhist shrine and temple, it garnered widespread reverence and thrived as the Ichinomiya of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita Districts. The shrine’s annual *Myōken Festival*, held on November 22–23, is recognized as one of the *Three Great Festivals of Kyushu* and designated as a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.From Yatsushiro Shrine historical records. == Enshrined Deities == * {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == Yatsushiro Myōken Festival == === National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property === The *Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* (八代妙見祭) is the shrine’s autumn grand festival and one of Kyushu’s Three Great Festivals.The Three Great Festivals of Kyushu are the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukuoka, and the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival. In some cases, {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} replaces Hōjō-e. Designated a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 2011 (Heisei 23), it was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 as part of the "Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals." The festival is the largest ritual in the Yatsushiro area, with records of its observance dating back to 1515 (Eishō 12) in the *Yatsushiro Nikki*. Historically, the procession carried the deity between the Lower and Middle Shrines. After a decline during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, it was revived under the patronage of the Kato clan and later the Hosokawa and Matsui clans.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=About the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} The festival features various traditional floats, including umbrellas, *kasaboko*, dragon and lion effigies, and a tortoise-serpent float inspired by the myth of {{ill|Genbu|ja|玄武|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=Myōken Festival Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} * November 22: *Oshitauri* (Descent) * November 23: *Oagari* (Ascent) == Himuro Festival == The *Himuro Festival* (氷室祭) is held annually from May 31 to June 1 to pray for good health and prosperity. {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} | location = 405 Myoken-cho, Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]]
[[Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] | shrine_Rank = Former prefectural shrine | founded = 795 CE (Enryaku 14) | associated = Myōken Shrine, Myōken-san | annual_festival = {{ill|Myōken Festival|ja|妙見祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ), also known as '''Myōken Shrine''' (みょうけんぐう) or '''Myōken-san,''' is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Yatsushiro City]], [[Kumamoto Prefecture]], Japan. Historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|State Shinto system]], it comprises three main shrines: the Upper Shrine, the Middle Shrine, and the Lower Shrine, with the Lower Shrine currently serving as the main sanctuary. Yatsushiro Shrine is counted among the "Three Great Myōken Shrines" of Japan alongside [[Sōma Nakamura Shrine]] in [[Fukushima Prefecture]] and {{ill|Nose Myōkenzan|fr}} in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == History == According to the ''Myōken Shrine Chronicle'' written in 1730 (Kyōhō 15), the shrine was first established as the Upper Shrine atop Mount Yokodake in 795 CE (Enryaku 14).{{Cite journal|和書|author=Hayase Terumi|title=囃されない笠鉾：八代妙見祭の笠鉾について|journal=造り物の文化史|date=2014|publisher=勉誠出版|isbn=9784585230281|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The Middle Shrine was constructed in 1160 CE (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was built in 1186 CE (Bunji 2) under the imperial command of [[Emperor Go-Toba]], with construction overseen by Kengyō Sanmi, Ōe no Ason Takafusa.Suzuki Kyō, ed. ''Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken Shrine. The deity [[Myōken]] symbolizes the [[Pole Star]] and the [[Big Dipper]]. The shrine functioned as a joint Shinto-Buddhist temple complex and was widely revered as the principal shrine (Ichinomiya) of the three districts of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita. Following the [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) policies of the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, with [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] and [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] enshrined as its primary deities.Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbun, ed. ''Kumamoto Prefecture Encyclopedia.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The annual ''Myōken Festival,'' held on [[November 22]]–[[November 23]], is one of the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''' and has been designated as an [[Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government.From the historical records of Yatsushiro Shrine. == Enshrined Deities == * [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] (天之御中主神) * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] (国常立尊) == Myōken Festival == === Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Designation) === The '''Myōken Festival''' (やつしろ みょうけんさい), held annually in the autumn, is among the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''', alongside the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.The "Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū" sometimes include {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead of the Hakozaki Shrine's Hōjō-e. The festival features a procession of floats and other ceremonial objects, some of which date back to the late Edo period. It was registered as part of UNESCO's [[Intangible Cultural Heritage]] in [[2016]] under the broader category of ''[[Yama, Hoko, Yatai, float festivals in Japan|Mountain, Float, and Procession Festivals]].''{{Cite web|和書|title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html|accessdate=2024-01-12}} The festival includes: * ''Oshimochi'' (Procession Downward) on [[November 22]] * ''Onobori'' (Procession Upward) on [[November 23]] == Himuro Festival == The '''Himuro Festival''' (ひむろまつり) is held annually from [[May 31]] to [[June 1]] at Yatsushiro Shrine. It is rooted in the early Edo period, when Yatsushiro Castle lord [[Hosokawa Tadaoki]] offered snow stored in the ice house of Mount Miroomiya to pray for good health.{{Cite web|和書|title=妙見さんの氷室祭り|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html|accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main Shrine Festivals == * Rice Planting Ceremony ([[January 3]]) * Seventeenth Night Festival ([[July 17]]) == Auxiliary Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Yamato Takeru]] * '''Inari Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama-no-Kami]] == Notable Structures == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken Shrine == Associated Shrines == === Reifu Shrine === * '''Deities''': Pole Star, Reifu Sonsei * '''Significance''': Reifu Shrine is an auxiliary shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine, revered as the head shrine of the deity {{ill|Jinchō Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of [[Empress Suiko]] by Prince [[Rinshō Taishi]] of [[Baekje]]. It is believed to bring prosperity and avert misfortune.Kumamoto Educational Association, ed. {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} | location = 405 Myoken-cho, Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]]
[[Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] | shrine_Rank = Former prefectural shrine | founded = 795 CE (Enryaku 14) | associated = Myōken Shrine, Myōken-san | annual_festival = {{ill|Myōken Festival|ja|妙見祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ), also known as '''Myōken Shrine''' (みょうけんぐう) or '''Myōken-san,''' is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Yatsushiro City]], [[Kumamoto Prefecture]], Japan. Historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|State Shinto system]], it comprises three main shrines: the Upper Shrine, the Middle Shrine, and the Lower Shrine, with the Lower Shrine currently serving as the main sanctuary. Yatsushiro Shrine is counted among the "Three Great Myōken Shrines" of Japan alongside [[Sōma Nakamura Shrine]] in [[Fukushima Prefecture]] and {{ill|Nose Myōkenzan|fr}} in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. == History == According to the ''Myōken Shrine Chronicle'' written in 1730 (Kyōhō 15), the shrine was first established as the Upper Shrine atop Mount Yokodake in 795 CE (Enryaku 14).{{Cite journal|和書|author=Hayase Terumi|title=囃されない笠鉾：八代妙見祭の笠鉾について|journal=造り物の文化史|date=2014|publisher=勉誠出版|isbn=9784585230281|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The Middle Shrine was constructed in 1160 CE (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was built in 1186 CE (Bunji 2) under the imperial command of [[Emperor Go-Toba]], with construction overseen by Kengyō Sanmi, Ōe no Ason Takafusa.Suzuki Kyō, ed. ''Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken Shrine. The deity [[Myōken]] symbolizes the [[Pole Star]] and the [[Big Dipper]]. The shrine functioned as a joint Shinto-Buddhist temple complex and was widely revered as the principal shrine (Ichinomiya) of the three districts of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita. Following the [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) policies of the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, with [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] and [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] enshrined as its primary deities.Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbun, ed. ''Kumamoto Prefecture Encyclopedia.'' Kumamoto Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The annual ''Myōken Festival,'' held on [[November 22]]–[[November 23]], is one of the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''' and has been designated as an [[Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government.From the historical records of Yatsushiro Shrine. == Enshrined Deities == * [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] (天之御中主神) * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kunino-Tokotachi-no-Kami]] (国常立尊) == Myōken Festival == === Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Designation) === The '''Myōken Festival''' (やつしろ みょうけんさい), held annually in the autumn, is among the '''Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū''', alongside the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.The "Three Great Festivals of Kyūshū" sometimes include {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead of the Hakozaki Shrine's Hōjō-e. The festival features a procession of floats and other ceremonial objects, some of which date back to the late Edo period. It was registered as part of UNESCO's [[Intangible Cultural Heritage]] in [[2016]] under the broader category of ''[[Yama, Hoko, Yatai, float festivals in Japan|Mountain, Float, and Procession Festivals]].''{{Cite web|和書|title=八代妙見祭の神幸行事とは?|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html|accessdate=2024-01-12}} The festival includes: * ''Oshimochi'' (Procession Downward) on [[November 22]] * ''Onobori'' (Procession Upward) on [[November 23]] == Himuro Festival == The '''Himuro Festival''' (ひむろまつり) is held annually from [[May 31]] to [[June 1]] at Yatsushiro Shrine. It is rooted in the early Edo period, when Yatsushiro Castle lord [[Hosokawa Tadaoki]] offered snow stored in the ice house of Mount Miroomiya to pray for good health.{{Cite web|和書|title=妙見さんの氷室祭り|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html|accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main Shrine Festivals == * Rice Planting Ceremony ([[January 3]]) * Seventeenth Night Festival ([[July 17]]) == Auxiliary Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Yamato Takeru]] * '''Inari Shrine''' : Enshrined deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama-no-Kami]] == Notable Structures == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken Shrine == Associated Shrines == === Reifu Shrine === * '''Deities''': Pole Star, Reifu Sonsei * '''Significance''': Reifu Shrine is an auxiliary shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine, revered as the head shrine of the deity {{ill|Jinchō Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of [[Empress Suiko]] by Prince [[Rinshō Taishi]] of [[Baekje]]. It is believed to bring prosperity and avert misfortune.Kumamoto Educational Association, ed. ''Yatsushiro District Chronicle,'' 1927, p. 396. == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine Official Page] (in Japanese) * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] (in Japanese) * {{Twitter|MyoukenKousiki}} * {{Facebook|myokensai}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Myōken Faith}} {{citation needed|Yatsushiro Shrine}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Otheruses|Yatsushiro Shrine in Kumamoto Prefecture}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Yatsushiro Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yatusiro jinja.JPG|260px]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=260|coord={{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E}}}} |location = {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Myōken-chō 405 |coordinates = {{coord|32.49984|N|130.64100|E|region:JP-43_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |shrine_Rank = Prefectural Shrine |founded = 795 (Enryaku 14) |main_hall = |alternate_names = Myōken-gū
Myōken-san |annual_festival = Myōken Festival |rites = }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Commonly known as '''Myōken-gū''' (妙見宮) or '''Myōken-san''', it was historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine comprises three precincts: the U11er Shrine (Kamimiya), Middle Shrine (Nakamiya), and Lower Shrine (Shimomiya). Currently, the Lower Shrine serves as the main shrine. Alongside {{ill|Sōma Myōken|ja|相馬妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukushima Prefecture and {{ill|Myōkenzan (Osaka and Hyōgo)|lt=Nose Myōken|ja|妙見山 (能勢)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Osaka Prefecture, it is considered one of the "Three Great Myōken Shrines of Japan." == History == According to the *Myōken-gū Jikki* (1730), the shrine was founded in 795 (Enryaku 14) at the summit of Yokodake, where the U11er Shrine was established. The Middle Shrine was built in 1160 (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was constructed in 1186 (Bunji 2) as an imperial prayer offering by Emperor Go-Toba, under the direction of Lord Ōe Takafusa.Takashi Suzuki (ed.), *Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken-gū. The deity {{ill|Myōken|ja|妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} symbolizes the North Star and the Big Di11er. As a dual Shinto-Buddhist shrine and temple, it garnered widespread reverence and thrived as the Ichinomiya of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita Districts. In 1871 (Meiji 4), due to the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhist separation|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the enshrined deities were identified as {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, attaining prefectural shrine status.*Kumamoto Prefectural Encyclopedia*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The shrine’s annual *Myōken Festival*, held on November 22–23, is recognized as one of the *Three Great Festivals of Kyushu* and designated as a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.From Yatsushiro Shrine historical records. == Enshrined Deities == * {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == Yatsushiro Myōken Festival == === National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property === The *Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* (八代妙見祭) is the shrine’s autumn grand festival and one of Kyushu’s Three Great Festivals.The Three Great Festivals of Kyushu are the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukuoka, and the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival. In some cases, {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} replaces Hōjō-e. Designated a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 2011 (Heisei 23), it was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 as part of the "Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals." The festival is the largest ritual in the Yatsushiro area, with records of its observance dating back to 1515 (Eishō 12) in the *Yatsushiro Nikki*. Historically, the procession carried the deity between the Lower and Middle Shrines. After a decline during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, it was revived under the patronage of the Kato clan and later the Hosokawa and Matsui clans.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=About the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} The festival features various traditional floats, including umbrellas, *kasaboko*, dragon and lion effigies, and a tortoise-serpent float inspired by the myth of {{ill|Genbu|ja|玄武|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=Myōken Festival Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} * November 22: *Oshitauri* (Descent) * November 23: *Oagari* (Ascent) == Himuro Festival == The *Himuro Festival* (氷室祭) is held annually from May 31 to June 1 to pray for good health and prosperity. It originates from a 17th-century tradition of offering snow stored in the local *himuro* (ice chamber) to the shrine by Yatsushiro Castle lord {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html |title=Myōken-san Himuro Festival (Kumamoto Prefecture Website) |accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main festivals == * '''Rice-Planting Ritual''' (January 3) * '''17th Night Festival''' (July 17) == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神|1=Ukemochi|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Grounds == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken-gū == External Subordinate Shrine == {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Reifu Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = {{image requested|cat=Yatsushiro}} |location = {{ill|Myōken-chō, Yatsushiro|ja|妙見町 (八代市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |coordinates = |enshrined_deities = North Star, Reifu deity |shrine_Rank = Main Shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |founded = Traditionally during the reign of Empress Suiko |main_hall = }} === Reifu Shrine === * '''Enshrined Deities''': North Star, Reifu deity * '''History''': Reifu Shrine (れいふじんじゃ) is a subordinate shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine and the principal shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the deity was introduced to Japan by {{ill|Prince Imseong|ja|琳聖太子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third prince of {{ill|Seong of Baekje|ja|聖王 (百済)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and enshrined at Myōken-gū. While the shrine deteriorated during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was restored during the Taishō period.*Yatsushiro District Records*, Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association, 1927. * '''location''': A11roximately 200 meters east of Yatsushiro Shrine. == References == == Further Reading == * Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association (ed.), *Yatsushiro District Records*, 1927 (Reprinted 1973, Rinsen Shoten). * Shirai Eiji, Toki Masanori (eds.), *Shinto Dictionary*, Tokyo-dō Publishing, 1979, p. 340. * Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Editorial Committee, *Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Vol. 43: Kumamoto Prefecture*, Kadokawa Shoten, 1987, 11. 1096–1097. * Kamiyama Haruhira et al., *Complete Overview of Japan’s Shrines*, Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha, 1992. * Yatsushiro City Board of Education (ed.), *The Myōken Festival of Yatsushiro: Cultural Property Survey Report No. 43*, 2010. * {{Cite journal |author = Hayase Terumi |title = *Kasaboko Without Festivity: On the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* |journal = Cultural History of Festival Structures |date = 2014 |publisher = Bensei Publishing |isbn = 9784585230281 |ref = harv }} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Shioya Hachiman Shrine|ja|塩屋八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html Myōken Festival Historical Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] * [https://twitter.com/MyoukenKousiki Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (@MyoukenKousiki) - Twitter] * [https://www.facebook.com/myokensai/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival - Facebook] {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{Redirect-related categories|redirect1=Procession of the Myōken Festival in Yatsushiro|1-1=Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やつしろしんしや}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)}} {{translated page|ja|八代神社|version=97899290|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:One Shrine per Province]] [[Category:Yatsushiro City]] [[Category:Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Japanese festivals]] [[Category:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:11]] [[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]][[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]]}} [[sn:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[de:Yatsushiro Shrine]] [[ja:八代神社]] [[sn:Reifu Shrine (Yatsushiro)]]

Myōken-san |annual_festival = Myōken Festival |rites = }} '''Yatsushiro Shrine''' (やつしろじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Yatsushiro|ja|八代市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Commonly known as '''Myōken-gū''' (妙見宮) or '''Myōken-san''', it was historically Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine comprises three precincts: the U11er Shrine (Kamimiya), Middle Shrine (Nakamiya), and Lower Shrine (Shimomiya). Currently, the Lower Shrine serves as the main shrine. Alongside {{ill|Sōma Myōken|ja|相馬妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukushima Prefecture and {{ill|Myōkenzan (Osaka and Hyōgo)|lt=Nose Myōken|ja|妙見山 (能勢)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Osaka Prefecture, it is considered one of the "Three Great Myōken Shrines of Japan." == History == According to the *Myōken-gū Jikki* (1730), the shrine was founded in 795 (Enryaku 14) at the summit of Yokodake, where the U11er Shrine was established. The Middle Shrine was built in 1160 (Eiryaku 1), and the Lower Shrine was constructed in 1186 (Bunji 2) as an imperial prayer offering by Emperor Go-Toba, under the direction of Lord Ōe Takafusa.Takashi Suzuki (ed.), *Kumamoto no Jinja to Tera*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1980, p. 90. Until 1870 (Meiji 3), the shrine was known as Myōken-gū. The deity {{ill|Myōken|ja|妙見|qq=draft|qq=draft}} symbolizes the North Star and the Big Di11er. As a dual Shinto-Buddhist shrine and temple, it garnered widespread reverence and thrived as the Ichinomiya of Yatsushiro, Shimo-Mashiki, and Ashikita Districts. In 1871 (Meiji 4), due to the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhist separation|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the enshrined deities were identified as {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and the shrine was renamed Yatsushiro Shrine, attaining prefectural shrine status.*Kumamoto Prefectural Encyclopedia*, Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbunsha, 1982, p. 456. The shrine’s annual *Myōken Festival*, held on November 22–23, is recognized as one of the *Three Great Festivals of Kyushu* and designated as a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.From Yatsushiro Shrine historical records. == Enshrined Deities == * {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto|ja|国常立尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == Yatsushiro Myōken Festival == === National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property === The *Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* (八代妙見祭) is the shrine’s autumn grand festival and one of Kyushu’s Three Great Festivals.The Three Great Festivals of Kyushu are the {{ill|Nagasaki Kunchi|ja|長崎くんち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Nagasaki)|ja|鎮西大社諏訪神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the {{ill|Hōjō-e|ja|放生会|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|ja|筥崎宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Fukuoka, and the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival. In some cases, {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|ja|博多祇園山笠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} replaces Hōjō-e. Designated a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 2011 (Heisei 23), it was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 as part of the "Yama, Hoko, and Yatai Festivals." The festival is the largest ritual in the Yatsushiro area, with records of its observance dating back to 1515 (Eishō 12) in the *Yatsushiro Nikki*. Historically, the procession carried the deity between the Lower and Middle Shrines. After a decline during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, it was revived under the patronage of the Kato clan and later the Hosokawa and Matsui clans.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji0031289/index.html |title=About the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} The festival features various traditional floats, including umbrellas, *kasaboko*, dragon and lion effigies, and a tortoise-serpent float inspired by the myth of {{ill|Genbu|ja|玄武|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html |title=Myōken Festival Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website) |accessdate=2016-04-22}} * November 22: *Oshitauri* (Descent) * November 23: *Oagari* (Ascent) == Himuro Festival == The *Himuro Festival* (氷室祭) is held annually from May 31 to June 1 to pray for good health and prosperity. It originates from a 17th-century tradition of offering snow stored in the local *himuro* (ice chamber) to the shrine by Yatsushiro Castle lord {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.kumamoto.jp/site/arinomama/myouhimuro.html |title=Myōken-san Himuro Festival (Kumamoto Prefecture Website) |accessdate=2014-02-12}} == Main festivals == * '''Rice-Planting Ritual''' (January 3) * '''17th Night Festival''' (July 17) == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōmiya Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食神|1=Ukemochi|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Grounds == * Six Jizō Statues of Myōken-gū == External Subordinate Shrine == {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Reifu Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = {{image requested|cat=Yatsushiro}} |location = {{ill|Myōken-chō, Yatsushiro|ja|妙見町 (八代市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|ja|熊本県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |coordinates = |enshrined_deities = North Star, Reifu deity |shrine_Rank = Main Shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |founded = Traditionally during the reign of Empress Suiko |main_hall = }} === Reifu Shrine === * '''Enshrined Deities''': North Star, Reifu deity * '''History''': Reifu Shrine (れいふじんじゃ) is a subordinate shrine of Yatsushiro Shrine and the principal shrine of {{ill|Chintaku Reifu Shin|ja|鎮宅霊符神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to tradition, the deity was introduced to Japan by {{ill|Prince Imseong|ja|琳聖太子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third prince of {{ill|Seong of Baekje|ja|聖王 (百済)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and enshrined at Myōken-gū. While the shrine deteriorated during the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|廃仏毀釈|1=Haibutsu kishaku|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was restored during the Taishō period.*Yatsushiro District Records*, Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association, 1927. * '''location''': A11roximately 200 meters east of Yatsushiro Shrine. == References == == Further Reading == * Kumamoto Prefectural Education Association (ed.), *Yatsushiro District Records*, 1927 (Reprinted 1973, Rinsen Shoten). * Shirai Eiji, Toki Masanori (eds.), *Shinto Dictionary*, Tokyo-dō Publishing, 1979, p. 340. * Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Editorial Committee, *Kadokawa Japan Place name Dictionary Vol. 43: Kumamoto Prefecture*, Kadokawa Shoten, 1987, 11. 1096–1097. * Kamiyama Haruhira et al., *Complete Overview of Japan’s Shrines*, Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha, 1992. * Yatsushiro City Board of Education (ed.), *The Myōken Festival of Yatsushiro: Cultural Property Survey Report No. 43*, 2010. * {{Cite journal |author = Hayase Terumi |title = *Kasaboko Without Festivity: On the Yatsushiro Myōken Festival* |journal = Cultural History of Festival Structures |date = 2014 |publisher = Bensei Publishing |isbn = 9784585230281 |ref = harv }} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Shioya Hachiman Shrine|ja|塩屋八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003640/index.html Yatsushiro Shrine (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.city.yatsushiro.lg.jp/bunka/kiji003312/index.html Myōken Festival Historical Materials (Yatsushiro City Official Website)] * [http://www.myouken.com/ Yatsushiro Myōken Festival Official Website] * [https://twitter.com/MyoukenKousiki Yatsushiro Myōken Festival (@MyoukenKousiki) -
